name: FAW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: FAW's top belt, and the one the fed kept through every rebuild it went through. Its first champion, HaHaKlown, is recorded as never having lost it — he handed it to his own sidekick Deadman and became president instead. Pyro took it at Breakaway 2001, American Psycho took it from Pyro, and from there it moved almost monthly: Spider, Spawn, Jim ‘JLC’ Phoenix, Skipster, The Omega Fro twice, The British Bomber, Chris Thunder for nine days in January 2002, Tony Vigilante, Rzarector through the summer of 2003, and Violator from Deceit on 9 November 2003. The fed's own paperwork survives in snapshots rather than as a ledger, so the order above is what its champions pages and its Hall of Fame between them attest, not a continuous chain.
notes: A separate, earlier champions snapshot of 8 April 2002 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-april-2002.html) names The Omega Fro as World Champion, International Champion EDH, European Champion Shifty, Hardcore Champion Xander, and Tag Team Champions Foam World Order (Neo & 9th Wonder Of Foam); all five corroborate reigns already recorded as open-ended at that date and do not themselves change any recorded date.

name: FAW International Championship
epitaph: The fed's secondary singles belt, and one of the three it kept when it cut its championship list down in 2003. Sean Mason defended it in Chris Thunder's own pay-per-view debut at Breakaway 2001; Jim ‘JLC’ Phoenix took it after eight months on the roster and called it the breakthrough of his career; Chris Thunder won it in a triple threat at Taking Hardcore To The Extreme in October 2001, in the match that started the xCw invasion, and lost it inside the month. Shifty held it in the summer of 2002. Sniper beat The British Bomber for it on the 6 July 2003 Panic and was still champion at the fed's last surviving snapshot that December.
notes: FAW's own champions page, June 2002 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-june-2002.html), FAW's own current-champions page, August 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-current-champions-august-2003.html), FAW's own champions page, December 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-december-2003.html) and FAW's own Hall of Fame page (promotions/faw/archive/faw-hall-of-fame.html).

name: FAW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Reinstated in the summer of 2001 and held by nearly every stable FAW ran. Dark Generation took the belts and were stripped of them when both champions were injured; Skipster and The Omega Fro, Chris Thunder with three different partners, the Mass Murderers, the Foam World Order and New School all held them across 2002. They were vacant going into Diabolical Day 2003, where a triple threat gave them to the Vice Squad — who were handed the belts and put on the floor with chairs in the same minute.
notes: FAW's own champions page, June 2002 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-june-2002.html), FAW's own current-champions page, August 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-current-champions-august-2003.html), FAW's own champions page, December 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-december-2003.html), FAW's own Hall of Fame page (promotions/faw/archive/faw-hall-of-fame.html) and FAW's own Diabolical Day 2003 recap (promotions/faw/archive/diabolical-day-2003-2003-07-13.html).

name: FAW Television Championship
epitaph: FAW retired this belt in memory of Joe “Soulja” Smallze, who wrestled here and died in April 2002. The fed's own champions page carried the line where a champion's name would go: “Retired in honour of Joe Smallze R.I.P”. It did not stay retired: by SummerSlaughter in August 2002 the fed had brought it back and put it on the line, over the objection of Smallze's own cousin Hardcore Hoefel, who stole the belt from champion Syd and buried it at Smallze's grave hours before Syd defended it anyway, losing it to J.J. Dynasty.

events.note: Retired unfilled in memory of Joe “Soulja” Smallze, who died in April 2002.

notes: FAW's own champions page, June 2002 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-june-2002.html), captured 10 June 2002. The same fact is independently recorded in the Primetime Central corpus already held.

name: FAW European Championship
epitaph: A mid-card singles belt through 2001 and 2002 — Jim ‘JLC’ Phoenix twice, Spawn, Skipster, Baz, Kryptonite, Shensui Yusuki, Shifty and Cyrus Skar all held it, and Joe La Fontaine was champion at the fed's own June 2002 snapshot. It is one of the five titles FAW's own 2003 champions page names as no longer worth keeping.
notes: FAW's own champions page, June 2002 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-june-2002.html), FAW's own champions page, December 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-december-2003.html) and the fed's own roster-database bio cards (faw.projectefed.com/cgi-bin/roster.cgi), workshop-held, never served.

events.note: Champion Cyrus Skar has the title discontinued on-air ("Europe is a waste of space") and replaced with a new FAW United States Championship; Tom "the Bomb" has the physical belt discarded and hands Skar the new US title instead. FAW Breakdown #1, read in full.

name: FAW Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The belt Apocalypse held six times. Skipster held it twice, Jim ‘JLC’ Phoenix twice, Baz twice, and Spider, Bayne and The Omega Fro once each; Violator was champion at the fed's own June 2002 snapshot. It was one of the titles dropped in the 2003 cut.
notes: FAW's own champions snapshot of 6 February 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-february-2003.html) names "Golden Nine" Jeff Harris as Hardcore Champion, narrowing the undocumented transition between Damien Ryan's 29 September 2002 win and Harris's own reign to on-or-before 6 February 2003 -- previously the transition was bounded only by Harris's confirmed title on 30 March 2003. A same-week Panic card (promotions/faw/archive/faw-panic-card-2003-02-02.html) bills a Hardcore Title triple threat, Jeff Harris vs Rzarector vs Skipster, corroborating the same snapshot; no results page for that card survives.

name: FAW Extreme Championship
epitaph: A short-lived belt of the 2003 era. The Meditator was champion going into Diabolical Day on 13 July 2003, where a fatal four-way with Khristian Call, Damien Ryan and Horazon ended with Call sitting on a broken ladder for the three-count. Call was still champion at the fed's own August 2003 snapshot; by December the title was gone from the fed's own list.
notes: FAW's own current-champions page, August 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-current-champions-august-2003.html), FAW's own champions page, December 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-december-2003.html) and FAW's own Diabolical Day 2003 recap (promotions/faw/archive/diabolical-day-2003-2003-07-13.html).

name: FAW Woman's Championship
epitaph: One champion survives in the record: Tanya Vigilante, on the fed's own June 2002 champions page. The title is named again only once more, in the 2003 list of belts FAW decided to stop defending.
notes: FAW's own champions page, June 2002 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-june-2002.html) and FAW's own champions page, December 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-december-2003.html).

name: FAW Continental Championship
epitaph: Named on FAW's own December 2002 title-history index as one of four belts whose recorded history began on 1 December 2002, and named again in the 2003 list of titles the fed stopped defending. The only holder the surviving record identifies is Dave Tronick, billed as a former Continental Champion on his own return at Diabolical Day 2003; the index page's own linked histories were never captured.
notes: FAW's own Title History index, December 2002 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-title-history-index.html), FAW's own champions page, December 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-december-2003.html) and FAW's own Diabolical Day 2003 recap (promotions/faw/archive/diabolical-day-2003-2003-07-13.html).

name: FAW Light-Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Chris Thunder was the first champion, in August 2001. No other holder appears anywhere in the surviving record, and the belt is absent from every later list of the fed's own championships.
notes: the fed's own roster-database bio cards (faw.projectefed.com/cgi-bin/roster.cgi), workshop-held, never served — Chris Thunder's own bio card: “became the first FAW Light-Heavyweight Champion”.

name: FAW Universal Championship
epitaph: Sat above the World Championship on FAW's own earliest surviving site. The Olympian held it first, into a March 2001 I Quit Match against Lex Luger; Luger carried it into a four-way battle royal at Extreme Beating and lost it there to British Bulldog, then held it again by the fed's own FAW is War card at month's end. A Tables, Ladders and Chairs rematch against Bulldog for it at May Day Massacre was called off on air for injuries to both men, and FAW's own president scrapped the belt that night — though the fed's own later site still names a champion for it into 2003.
notes: FAW's own champions page, dated March 2001 and captured 21 April 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-2001-03.html); its own cards page, same snapshot (promotions/faw/archive/faw-cards-2001-03.html); Tuesday Torture, 20 March 2001, Friday Night Fear, 23 March 2001, Extreme Beating, March 2001, FAW is War, 30 April 2001, and May Day Massacre, 5 May 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/tuesday-torture-2001-03-20.html, friday-night-fear-2001-03-23.html, extreme-beating-2001-03.html, faw-is-war-2001-04-30.html, may-day-massacre-2001-05-05.html and may-day-massacre-card-2001-05-05.html). FAW's ten registered titles do not include this belt. This crawl's own full 2003 read (When Worlds Collide 2003, Panic (February and 6 April), Extreme Beating Three) turned up Sean Mason billed champion throughout but found no textual support anywhere for this note's own earlier claim that Xander was separately billed champion -- that claim could not be corroborated and may be an error in this row's own prior research pass.

name: FAW United States Championship
epitaph: Created on FAW's own first Breakdown to replace the discontinued European Championship, at reigning European Champion Cyrus Skar's own request; Skar became its first holder without a match.

name: Diabolical Day King
epitaph: The tournament FAW ran on its own Diabolical Day pay-per-view every July, and the title its winner carried for the year: Diabolical Day King. The winner took a World Championship shot with it — in 2001 on the following night's FAW is WAR, in 2003 at Collision Course.
